It discusses the potential impact of ongoing IRS audits and the implications of tax positions on the company's effective tax rate. The section also outlines the tax filing practices of Corning Incorporated and its subsidiaries, including the status of audits and appeals in various jurisdictions. Additionally, it mentions the company's reserves for uncertain tax positions and the likelihood of changes in these amounts over the next year.

children.title: Property, Plant and Equipment Overview
children.summary: This section provides a detailed breakdown of property, plant, and equipment (PP&E) net of accumulated depreciation for the years ending December 31, 2021, and 2020. It includes specific values for land, buildings, equipment, and construction in progress, totaling $15.8 billion in 2021. The section also notes the accumulated depreciation amounting to approximately $14 billion. Additionally, it highlights the capitalization of interest costs related to PP&E and the recorded value of precious metals in manufacturing equipment, along with depletion expenses for these metals over the past three years.

children.title: Goodwill and Intangible Assets Overview
children.summary: This section provides an overview of Corning's goodwill and intangible assets, detailing the changes in goodwill carrying amounts for 2020 and 2021 across business segments. It reports a total goodwill balance of $2.421 billion as of December 31, 2021, and discusses impairment losses, particularly in the Optical Communications segment. Additionally, it breaks down other intangible assets such as patents and customer lists, including their net values and amortization schedules, and outlines expected annual amortization expenses for the next five years.

children.title: Goodwill and Intangible Assets Overview
children.summary: This section details the changes in the carrying amount of goodwill for Corning over the years 2020 and 2021, including specific figures for each business segment. It highlights the total goodwill balance, which was $2.421 billion as of December 31, 2021, and discusses accumulated impairment losses primarily affecting the Optical Communications segment. Additionally, it provides a breakdown of other intangible assets, including patents and customer lists, with net values and amortization details. The section also outlines expected annual amortization expenses for the next five years.

children.title: Overview of Other Assets and Liabilities
children.summary: This section details the company's other assets and liabilities as of December 31 for the years 2021 and 2020. It includes current and non-current assets such as derivative instruments, South Korean tax deposits, and operating leases, with total other assets amounting to $2,056 million in 2021. The liabilities section outlines current and non-current obligations, including wages, income taxes, and defined benefit pension plan liabilities, totaling $5,192 million in 2021. The section also highlights ongoing tax appeals in South Korea and provides references to related notes for further details.

children.title: Corning's Debt Maturities and Management Overview
children.summary: This section provides an overview of Corning's debt maturities as of December 31, 2021, detailing annual amounts due from 2022 onwards. It highlights significant debt issuances and repayments from 2020 and 2021, including the redemption of debentures and related losses. Additionally, it discusses borrowings under unsecured variable rate loan facilities in Chinese yuan and Japanese yen, noting that these loans lack guarantees from other Corning entities. The section also covers the company's debt management strategies and financial obligations during the specified periods.

children.title: Corning's Debt Maturities and Management Overview
children.summary: This section details Corning's debt maturities as of December 31, 2021, including specific amounts due each year from 2022 to thereafter. It outlines significant debt issuances and repayments in 2021 and 2020, highlighting the redemption of debentures and associated losses. The section also mentions borrowings under unsecured variable rate loan facilities, including amounts in Chinese yuan and Japanese yen, and notes that these loans are not guaranteed by other Corning entities. Readers can learn about the company's debt management strategies and financial obligations over the specified periods.

children.title: Overview of Employee Retirement Plans and Financials
children.summary: This section covers the funded status and financials of employee retirement plans, including defined benefit pension and post-retirement benefits. It provides year-over-year comparisons of obligations and assets, detailing actuarial gains and losses, and net periodic benefit expenses. Corning's valuation methodology, investment strategy, and fair value measurements of plan assets are discussed, along with associated risks and expected benefit payments. Specific figures for accumulated benefit obligations and investment allocations are included for the years 2020 and 2021.

children.title: Overview of Employee Retirement Plans' Funded Status
children.summary: This section details the obligations and funded status of defined benefit pension and post-retirement benefit plans, providing a year-over-year comparison of benefit obligations and plan assets. It includes specific figures for domestic and international pension benefits, as well as post-retirement benefits for the years 2020 and 2021. Key components such as service costs, interest costs, actuarial gains and losses, and benefits paid are outlined, along with the fair value of plan assets and the resulting funded status. The section also highlights amounts recognized in the consolidated balance sheets and accumulated other comprehensive loss, offering insights into the financial health of the retirement plans.

children.title: Overview of Employee Retirement Plan Financials
children.summary: This section details the actuarial gains and losses related to employee retirement plans, highlighting a $124 million gain in 2021 due to increased bond yields, contrasting with a $358 million loss in 2020. It provides specific figures for the accumulated benefit obligation for defined benefit pension plans, which were $4.5 billion in 2021 and $4.7 billion in 2020. The section also outlines the components of net periodic benefit expense for domestic and international pension benefits, as well as postretirement benefits, including service costs, interest costs, and expected returns on plan assets. Additionally, it discusses changes in plan assets and benefit obligations recognized in other comprehensive income.

children.title: Corning's Employee Retirement Plan Valuation and Investment Strategy
children.summary: This section details Corning's methodology for discounting projected benefit payments in employee retirement plans using a hypothetical yield curve based on high-quality corporate bonds. It explains the importance of mortality assumptions in valuing retirement plan liabilities, including updates to mortality tables and improvement scales. The section also provides weighted-average assumptions for pension benefits, including discount rates and expected returns on plan assets for the years 2019-2021. Additionally, it outlines the company's investment strategy for plan assets, emphasizing liquidity and diversification through public securities, with specific target allocations for equity and bond investments.

children.title: Employee Retirement Plans Fair Value and Risks
children.summary: This section provides detailed fair value measurement information for the Company's defined benefit plan assets, categorized into Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3 inputs. It includes specific data on domestic and international equity securities, fixed income, private equity, and real estate investments as of December 31 for 2021 and 2020. Additionally, it discusses risks associated with these investments, including credit, currency, and liquidity risks. The section also outlines expected gross benefit payments for domestic and international pension plans and postretirement benefits for the years 2022 to 2031, along with defined contribution plan expenses for recent years.

children.title: Overview of Commitments and Contingencies
children.summary: This section details the company's commitments, contingencies, and guarantees, including financial obligations categorized by expiration periods. It provides specific amounts for performance bonds, letters of credit, purchase obligations, and capital expenditure obligations, totaling over $18 billion. The company recognizes liabilities for guarantees issued and notes that most guarantees are not significant and are expected to expire without funding. Additionally, it discusses the limited ability of subsidiaries to transfer funds due to regulatory and contractual restrictions, and mentions ongoing lawsuits with a low likelihood of materially affecting the company's financial position.

children.title: Overview of Commitments and Contingencies
children.summary: This section details Corning's commitments, contingencies, and guarantees, including financial obligations such as performance bonds, letters of credit, purchase obligations, and capital expenditure obligations, totaling over $18 billion. It outlines the company's indemnity obligations related to Dow Corning's liabilities, including breast implant litigation and environmental claims, and discusses the company's approach to recognizing liabilities for guarantees issued. Additionally, it addresses the company's involvement in various lawsuits and environmental litigation, emphasizing that management believes the likelihood of material adverse effects on financial position is remote.

children.title: Corning's Foreign Currency Hedging Activities
children.summary: This section discusses Corning's hedging activities to mitigate foreign currency risks primarily related to the Japanese yen, South Korean won, new Taiwan dollar, Chinese yuan, euro, and British pound. It details the use of over-the-counter derivative instruments, including foreign exchange forward and option contracts, to manage cash flow and fair value risks. The section also outlines the notional values of these hedges, the assessment of hedge effectiveness, and the potential risks associated with counterparty non-performance. Additionally, it provides financial data on gains and losses from these hedging activities as recorded in the consolidated financial statements.

children.title: Overview of Fair Value Measurements Standards
children.summary: This section outlines the fair value measurement standards under U.S. GAAP, defining fair value and establishing a framework for its measurement. It distinguishes between observable and unobservable inputs used to determine fair value, categorizing them into three levels: Level 1 (quoted market prices), Level 2 (significant observable inputs), and Level 3 (significant unobservable inputs). The section also provides specific fair value measurement data for the company's financial assets and liabilities, including details on impairments and disposals related to long-lived assets. Additionally, it highlights the importance of using observable market data when available for fair value assessments.

children.title: Overview of Shareholders' Equity and Dividends
children.summary: This section details Corning's shareholders' equity, focusing on common stock dividends, preferred stock conversions, and share repurchases. It highlights the 13% increase in quarterly common stock dividends declared in February 2022, marking the eleventh increase since 2011. The conversion of 2,300 shares of preferred stock into common shares and the subsequent repurchase of 35 million common shares for approximately $1.5 billion are also discussed. Additionally, it provides a summary of accumulated other comprehensive loss and reclassifications out of accumulated other comprehensive income, detailing changes in components such as foreign currency translation adjustments and actuarial gains or losses.

children.title: Earnings Per Common Share Calculation and Analysis
children.summary: This section details the calculation of basic and diluted earnings per common share for Corning Incorporated. Basic earnings are derived from net income available to common shareholders divided by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding, while diluted earnings account for potentially dilutive securities. The section provides a reconciliation of net income figures for the years 2019 to 2021, including adjustments for preferred stock dividends and redemptions. It also discusses the impact of the conversion of Series A preferred stock into common shares on earnings calculations. Additionally, it notes the exclusion of anti-dilutive shares from the diluted earnings per share calculation.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Share-Based Compensation Plans
children.summary: This section provides a comprehensive overview of Corning's share-based compensation practices, detailing various stock compensation plans including stock options, restricted stock units, and performance-based awards. It covers the measurement and recognition of compensation costs, the treatment of forfeitures, and the accounting implications for each type of award. Financial figures related to total compensation costs, stock options outstanding, and vesting schedules are included, along with specific data on exercise prices and intrinsic values as of December 31, 2021. The section emphasizes the fair value determination and vesting periods associated with different equity awards.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Stock Compensation Plans
children.summary: This section details Corning's stock compensation plans, which include various equity-based awards such as stock options and restricted stock units for employees and board members. It explains the measurement and recognition of compensation costs based on estimated fair values, including the treatment of forfeitures. The section provides financial figures for total share-based compensation costs and tax benefits over three years, as well as specific data on stock options outstanding, including exercise prices and intrinsic values as of December 31, 2021.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Stock Option Plans
children.summary: This section details Corning's stock option plans, which include non-qualified and incentive stock options for purchasing common shares at market price on the grant date. It explains the vesting schedule, which typically spans from one to five years, and the maximum term of options, which is ten years. The section also provides a summary of stock options outstanding as of December 31, 2021, including the number of shares, exercise prices, and intrinsic values, along with historical data on exercised and forfeited options. Additionally, it outlines the accounting treatment for stock options and the impact on share-based compensation costs.

children.title: Overview of Corning's Incentive Stock Plans
children.summary: The Corning Incentive Stock Plan allows for grants of restricted stock and restricted stock units, which may be tied to performance goals or issued directly. These grants are typically subject to forfeiture and do not require cash consideration. The fair value of these awards is determined by the stock's closing market price on the grant date, with vesting periods ranging from one to ten years. Compensation costs are recognized over the vesting period and adjusted for any forfeitures that occur before vesting.

children.title: Time-Based Restricted Stock and RSUs Overview
children.summary: This section discusses time-based restricted stock and restricted stock units (RSUs) issued by the Company, which are granted at the discretion of the Company and payable in shares upon vesting. The fair value of these awards is determined by the closing market price of the Company's stock on the grant date. Compensation costs associated with these awards are recognized over the vesting period and adjusted for any actual forfeitures that occur before vesting. Readers can learn about the valuation and accounting treatment of these stock-based compensation forms.

children.title: Overview of Performance-Based Restricted Stock Units
children.summary: This section discusses performance-based restricted stock units (PRSUs), which are granted based on the achievement of specific performance targets and typically vest over three years. The fair value of these units is determined by the market price of the company's stock at the grant date, assuming target performance will be met. Compensation costs for PRSUs are recognized over the vesting period and adjusted for actual forfeitures and changes in expected performance outcomes. Readers can learn about the accounting treatment and implications of PRSUs in the context of share-based compensation.

children.title: Financial Performance and Reconciliation of Reportable Segments
children.summary: This section covers the financial performance and reconciliation of reportable segments for the years 2019 to 2021, including net sales, income, and asset values. It details the impact of foreign currency movements, customer contracts, and unallocated expenses on consolidated results. Additionally, it provides insights into revenue from various product lines and geographic areas, highlighting trends in financial metrics and asset categories. The data emphasizes the overall financial health and operational distribution of the company across segments and regions.

children.title: Financial Performance of Reportable Segments
children.summary: This section details the financial performance of various reportable segments for the years ended December 31, 2019, 2020, and 2021. It includes segment net sales, depreciation, research and development expenses, income tax provisions, net income or loss, investments in affiliated companies, segment assets, and capital expenditures. The earnings of equity affiliates are incorporated into the respective segment's net income, and common expenses are allocated differently than for standalone financials. The data highlights trends and variations in financial metrics across segments over the specified years.

children.title: Reconciliation of Reportable Segments to Consolidated Sales
children.summary: This section provides a reconciliation of reportable segments and 'All Other' net sales to consolidated net sales for the years 2019 to 2021, detailing the impact of foreign currency movements and a cumulative adjustment related to a customer contract. It also reconciles net income of reportable segments to consolidated net income, highlighting various unallocated amounts such as foreign currency impacts, litigation expenses, and research costs. Key figures include net sales of $14,082 million in 2021 and net income of $1,906 million. The section emphasizes the financial performance and adjustments affecting the company's overall results.

children.title: Reconciliation of Reportable Segment Assets
children.summary: This section provides a reconciliation of reportable segment assets to the consolidated total assets for the years 2019 to 2021. It details the total assets of reportable segments, all other assets, and unallocated amounts, including current assets, investments, property, plant and equipment, and other non-current assets. The data is presented in millions and highlights changes in asset values over the three years. Additionally, it clarifies the nature of various asset categories, such as corporate investments and property not tied to specific operating segments.

children.title: Financial Overview of Reportable Segments
children.summary: This section provides detailed financial information on the Company's reportable segments, including revenue from external customers for the years 2019 to 2021 across various product lines such as Display Technologies, Optical Communications, Specialty Materials, Environmental Technologies, and Life Sciences. It also includes net sales and long-lived assets by geographic area, highlighting performance in North America, Asia Pacific, and Europe. The data reveals trends in revenue growth and the impact of foreign currency movements, as well as adjustments related to customer contracts. Readers can learn about the financial health and geographic distribution of the Company's operations.

children.title: Corning Subsidiaries and Equity Method Companies
children.summary: Exhibit 21 lists the subsidiaries of Corning Incorporated as of December 31, 2021, detailing their locations, including multiple entities in China, Delaware, and other countries. It also identifies companies accounted for under the equity method, such as Chengdu Honing Display Glass Co., Ltd. and Samsung Corning Advanced Glass LLC. Additionally, the section notes that summary financial information for these equity basis companies is available in Note 3 of the Consolidated Financial Statements. Certain non-significant subsidiaries are omitted from this exhibit as per regulatory guidelines.

children.title: Consent of Independent Accounting Firm for Financial Reporting
children.summary: This section contains the consent of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, to incorporate their report by reference in various Registration Statements for Corning Incorporated. The report, dated February 14, 2022, pertains to the financial statements and the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting. This consent is a formal acknowledgment necessary for regulatory compliance regarding the financial disclosures of the company.

children.title: CEO Certification Under Sarbanes-Oxley Act
children.summary: Exhibit 31.1 contains the certification of Wendell P. Weeks, the CEO of Corning Incorporated, in compliance with Section 302(a) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. The certification confirms that he has reviewed the Annual Report on Form 10-K and asserts that the report is free of material misstatements. It also details the responsibilities of the CEO regarding the establishment and maintenance of disclosure controls and internal controls over financial reporting. Furthermore, it includes an evaluation of the effectiveness of these controls and disclosures of any significant deficiencies or fraud related to financial reporting.

children.title: CFO Certification Under Sarbanes-Oxley Act
children.summary: Exhibit 31.2 contains the certification of R. Tony Tripeny, Chief Financial Officer of Corning Incorporated, in compliance with Section 302(a) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. The certification confirms that he has reviewed the annual report on Form 10-K and asserts that the report is free from material misstatements. It also details the responsibilities for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and internal controls over financial reporting. Additionally, it includes an evaluation of the effectiveness of these controls and disclosures of any significant deficiencies or fraud related to financial reporting.

children.title: CEO and CFO Certification of Financial Report Compliance
children.summary: Exhibit 32 contains the certification by Wendell P. Weeks, CEO, and R. Tony Tripeny, CFO, of Corning Incorporated, affirming compliance with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. The certification states that the company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ending December 31, 2021, meets the requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. It also asserts that the financial information presented in the report accurately reflects the company's financial condition and operational results. This section underscores the accountability of the company's executives regarding financial reporting.
